title: University machine-learning final exam series
summary: Students solve multi-part final-exam questions spanning machine-learning theory, mathematics, natural language, and code implementation. Researchers used 646 authentic question parts from MIT, Harvard, and Cornell to test language-model solving and question generation, showing that these exams are also vulnerable to external AI assistance.

sources.title: From Human Days to Machine Seconds: Automatically Answering and Generating Machine Learning Final Exams
sources.evidence_quote: One contribution of this work is the dataset of final questions derived from three courses: Introduction to Machine Learning at MIT and Cornell and Machine Learning at Harvard.

course.name: Introduction to Machine Learning
course.institution: MIT, Harvard University, and Cornell University

prerequisites: Programming fundamentals or introduction to algorithms

assessment.summary: Solve cumulative, timed machine-learning final questions that combine theory, mathematics, code, and multi-step reasoning.
student_actions: Solve open-ended and selected-response questions across a semester of machine learning.
Provide theory, mathematical, and code-implementation answers.

student_role.description: The authentic exams predate or do not report student AI use; the researchers submitted their questions to GPT-3, OPT, Codex, and ChatGPT as an assessment-security benchmark.

grading.method: Human and automatic grading, depending on question type.

provenance.extraction_method: Full PDF read from pdftotext output.
